edge_explainer: Answers the queue's question directly: the falling knife is NOT an estimates knife, it is a MARGIN knife. The 2026-07-23 FQ1-FY27 print was a double beat with RAISED full-year EPS guidance and the stock still fell 6.1%. Audited XBRL: revenue $1,020M +5.7% (down from +17% in the year-ago quarter) but OPERATING INCOME -6.1% and operating margin -190bps to 15.2%; diluted EPS +1.1% only because buyback offset net income -6.5%. So sell-side forward EPS is +19% ($8.36 vs $7.03 trailing) while the operating line is negative - estimates and operations point in opposite directions, and the de-rate is the market discounting the estimate line toward the operating line. Legitimate de-rate (quality intact: 57.8% GM, 6.4% FCF yield, net cash $1,131M verified before the EV claim, 11.9x forward) but NOT the HUBS/CTSH/SAP pattern, which requires stable-or-rising estimates with a stable operating line. Half-winner, half-warning. Peer tape rules out sector beta: DECK -12.4% 12mo vs ONON -23.9%, NKE -44.3%. TOP UNVERIFIABLE: the actual FY-2027 guidance numbers and the Hoka/UGG brand split were not read from primary - 'raised EPS guidance' and 'Hoka deceleration' are headline-sourced, and the Hoka kill trigger currently has no verified series to measure against.
